idiom_name: view interface + presenter + model, view double for tests
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: declare the view as a narrow interface in the screen's own vocabulary (never widgets or toolkit types), give the presenter an injected view and model, and have every gesture first reach the view and then be forwarded to a presenter method - the presenter does all reading of the view, all model interaction and all writing back to the view. Keep a second implementation of the view interface as a test double that records calls and answers queries, so the presenter needs no UI framework at all. Decide per screen between the Passive View form (presenter performs even simple field updates) and the Supervising Controller form (the view maps simple values itself, the presenter handles input response and complex logic), and define detach semantics for the view/presenter pair so recreated screens do not leak listeners.
code_sketch:
interface View:
    displayTotal(total)          # semantic, not setLabelText
    query() -> string

Presenter(view, model):
    onQueryChanged():
        total = model.total(view.query())
        view.displayTotal(total)     # presenter drives; view never reads the model

# tests: Presenter(RecordingView(), FakeModel()).onQueryChanged()
pitfalls: Exposing widget-level operations through the view interface instead of screen semantics re-couples the presenter to the concrete UI and destroys the multi-front-end reuse the pattern exists for.
Shipping without a view double: tests then drive the real window through the presenter and inherit the very framework dependency the pattern removes.
Forgetting detach: a view (or its event subscriptions) kept alive by the presenter outlives the screen, and a presenter kept alive by the view survives recreation with stale model references.

Wrong move: make the presenter a proxy for every model or service call -> domain rules leak into presentation and presenter tests become a brittle mirror -> instead keep business decisions in the model or application layer and translate only screen intent and results.

Wrong move: let widget-level presenters call one another across a large view -> ownership and lifecycle become a tangled dependency graph -> instead keep one presenter per screen or component boundary and coordinate shared state through the model or an event boundary.

Wrong move: impose a pure framework-agnostic MVP scaffold on every tiny component -> interface and file overhead obscures simple UI logic -> instead start with the smallest cohesive component and extract a contract when complexity, reuse or test isolation justifies it.
